venue.name: Beacon Hill Children's Farm
venue.description: The Beacon Hill Children's Farm is a small family-run farm inside Beacon Hill Park in Victoria that is home to more than a hundred farm animals, including goats, pigs, Jacob sheep, miniature donkeys, guinea pigs, alpacas, ducks, chickens, budgies, a conure, finches, pheasants and doves. It has been operated since 1985 by the Koenders family in conjunction with the Beacon Hill Farm Society. Admission is by donation, with suggested amounts of $6.00 for adults and $5.00 for children. Visitors may pet any animals at the fence who wish to be pet, and the goat petting area is the only animal enclosure they can enter.

facility_notes.washrooms: There is no bathroom inside the farm. Please plan enough time to take your group to the bathroom (walking distance around 3 minutes).
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: All of the paths inside the farm are gravel, with no steep inclines and no stairs.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is a parking lot directly outside the farm, along Circle Drive.

restrictions: No feeding any of the animals.
Walking only inside the farm: no running, jumping, or chasing after any animal.
No climbing on fences or goat climbing structures.
Quiet voices at all times: no yelling or shouting at the animals or other people.
Children must be supervised throughout their entire visit; close supervision in small groups is required while in the goat petting area.
No human food inside the goat area.
No picking up or restraining the goats.
All dogs must remain on a leash at all times, please no barking, and dogs may not enter the goat petting area.
venue.seasonal_notes: The farm runs a public season and an off season. The Plan Your Visit page still reads "The farm is open now for the season 2024!", so that page appears not to have been updated for the current year.

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: School, childcare and summer camp groups, and any group of 10 or more participants or requiring supervision, are asked to book ahead because there is a maximum capacity for the farm and the goat petting area; booked groups get priority on busy days. Inquiries go by email (with a phone number for a call back) or by phone at 250-381-2532, and should include the group name, a phone number, the number of children and accompanying supervisors, and the day and time you would like to visit. Admission is by donation with suggested amounts of $6.00 for adults and $5.00 for children; no group or school rate is published.
programs.what_children_do: Walk gravel paths past goats, pigs, sheep, miniature donkeys, alpacas and birds, petting any animals at the fence who want to be petted, then go into the goat petting area in small supervised groups. No feeding the animals, and quiet voices throughout.
programs.our_note: There is no washroom inside the farm and the nearest one is about three minutes' walk, so take the group before you go in. Staff will step in if the noise level rises, and a group that keeps at it can be asked to leave the goat area or the farm.
programs.practical_summary: No washroom on site - the nearest is about three minutes away on foot - and there is a parking lot directly outside on Circle Drive. Admission is by donation with no group rate published, and opening hours, season dates, visit length and the capacity of the goat area are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is by donation. The suggested amounts are $6.00 for adults and $5.00 for children.
programs.evidence: For school, childcare, or summer camp groups – or any group with 10 or more participants and those requiring supervision
